subject: Business Models
title: Netflix: DVD to Streaming
description: A micro-lesson that makes Netflix: DVD to Streaming usable.

hook.text: Netflix mailed DVDs in red envelopes. Then it bet the company on streaming and killed its own DVD business.

buildup.text: In 2007, Netflix launched streaming alongside DVD rental. Customers could do both for one price.

discovery.text: Netflix split the services and raised prices in 2011. It lost 800,000 subscribers in one quarter. Wall Street panicked.

twist.text: CEO Reed Hastings held firm. By 2013 Netflix was producing original content. By 2020 it had 200 million subscribers.

climax.text: Netflix cannibalized its own profitable model to build a bigger one. DVDs died, streaming became a $30B business.

punchline.text: Killed its own DVD business. Built a $30B streaming empire. Disruption wins.

quiz.question: How many subscribers did Netflix lose when it split DVDs and streaming?

details.summary: Netflix transformed three times: from DVD-by-mail eliminating late fees, to streaming eliminating physical media, to original content eliminating licensing dependency. Each pivot required cannibalizing its own successful model before competitors could.
details.whyItMatters: Netflix is the premier example of serial business model innovation. Its willingness to disrupt its own profitable model before external threats forced the change is a masterclass in strategic self-cannibalization.
takeaways: Netflix disrupted its own DVD business by launching streaming in 2007
Original content production reduced dependence on licensed programming
Each pivot cannibalized current revenue to capture future market position

faq.question: Why did Netflix invest in original content instead of continuing to license?
faq.answer: Content owners began launching their own streaming services, pulling licenses from Netflix. Disney, Warner, and NBC all withdrew content. Netflix needed proprietary content that competitors could not take away, making original production a strategic necessity.

faq.question: What can other companies learn from Netflix's model transitions?
faq.answer: Start building the next model while the current one is still profitable. Accept short-term financial pain for long-term positioning. Test new models at small scale before full commitment. The biggest risk is not cannibalization but being disrupted by someone else.
